title: Constant difference: ages in some years' time
question: Mr Ismail is 41 years old and his son is 9 years old. In how many years' time will Mr Ismail be 3 times as old as his son?

relations.from: Mr Ismail be 3 times as old as his son

timeline.say: Mr Ismail is 41 years old and his son is 9 years old. In how many years' time will Mr Ismail be 3 times as old as his son?
Mr Ismail is 41 years old now.
His son is 9 years old now.
Let's draw their ages now.
The son's bar is 9 years.
Mr Ismail's bar is 9 years plus the difference in their ages.
The difference in their ages is 41 minus 9, which is 32.
The difference is 32 years, and it never changes.

timeline.text: 3 times as old as his son
timeline.say: Later, Mr Ismail will be 3 times as old as his son.
Let's draw their ages at that time.
The son's bar grows by some years. His age then is 1 unit.
Mr Ismail's age then is 3 units.
His bar is 1 unit plus 2 units of difference.
The difference is still 32 years, and now it is 2 units.
We want the number of years that pass.
Pause and think. What is 1 unit worth?
2 units are 32 years.
So 1 unit is 32 divided by 2, which is 16.
1 unit is 16, so the son will be 16 years old.
He is 9 now, so 16 minus 9 is 7 years.
Let's check: in 7 years Mr Ismail is 48 and his son is 16. 48 is 3 times 16!

timeline.text: In 7 years' time, Mr Ismail will be 3 times as old as his son.
timeline.say: So, in 7 years' time, Mr Ismail will be 3 times as old as his son. Well done!
